summary: Cheap to build, but demand for prevention (vs. cure after a suspension) is unproven, Google's triggers are unknown so the checks are guesses, and three cheap incumbents exist. David has no Shopify network to reach buyers.

demand.evidence: One Shopify Community thread shows post-suspension pain; RESEARCH.md admits no merchant says they pay monthly for prevention. Vendor stats are unsourced.

statusQuo.evidence: Fiverr fixers $50-$400 and GMC.APPS $9-$99/mo show people pay after a suspension; that one-off cure undercuts a $15/mo subscription for a rare event.

specificity.evidence: Target is a category (Shopify owner-operators and agencies), no named person or agency; the painful moment calls for a fix, not a monitor.

wedge.evidence: A free scan page plus snapshot diff is weekend-sized, but value depends on checks that may not predict suspensions (one reply says it is account-level trust).

futureFit.evidence: Real signal lives in the Content API and Shopify/Google or GMC.APPS can add alerts natively; public-page checks have no moat.

premises: Merchants pay for prevention, not just cure: unsupported, all spend evidence is post-suspension.
Public storefront signals predict Misrepresentation suspensions: weakly supported by forum and vendor lists only.
$15/mo per store is the right price: unsupported, GMC.APPS starts at $9 and one-off fixes are cheap.
David can reach Shopify merchants without a network: plausible via Reddit/Community but cold.
alternatives: Minimal: free GMC trust-check scan page, no accounts, collect URLs and emails.
Ideal: Merchant Center Content API account watch; real signal but needs Google OAuth verification, not weekend-sized.
Lateral: $29 one-off pre-flight audit sold to agencies before any subscription.
Extend existing repo: none overlap; permitly's page-change diff technique could share a library.
wedge: A single free scan page running the 5 public checks against a Shopify URL, with an optional email-me-on-change box; no accounts or billing.

feasibility.notes: Next.js + cheerio + Turso/SQLite + Resend free + GitHub Actions cron, no LLM. Proving test: diffSnapshots(compliant, broken) returns exactly returns-policy and contact-details. That proves the code, not that the checks predict suspensions.

risks: Prevention demand unproven; buyers may only pay after a suspension for a cheaper one-off tool.
Checks are guesses; an all-green result followed by a suspension is a trust liability.
At least three cheap incumbents; GMC.APPS already advertises monitoring.
Shopify or Google can ship the same alerts natively.
No Shopify network; communities punish promotion and buyers search at the cure moment.
killCriteria: Under 50 qualified visitors or under 5% signups with a store URL in 14 days; fewer than 3 of 10 merchants say they would pay $15/mo for prevention; a competitor or Shopify ships monitoring; public checks would have caught fewer than half of 10 real reported suspensions.
